title: Now in Nature: Retrofitting language models to operate over bytes
key_facts: Ai2's Bolmo research on byte-level language models has been published in Nature; new checkpoints are on Hugging Face.
Byteifying turns an already capable subword model into a byte-level one with a relatively short extra training run.
The same process applied to Qwen 3 8B and Llama 3 8B gave Bwen 8B and Blama 8B, both close to the models they came from.
Bwen 8B is Ai2's strongest byteified model yet, outperforming Bolmo 7B across Ai2's aggregate evaluation suite.
Byte-level models read the bytes computers use for characters instead of a fixed vocabulary of word chunks.
Ai2 also released Stage 1 checkpoints, which keep the global model frozen while training the new byte-level parts.
quote_evidence: We created a process we call byteifying, which takes an already capable subword model and converts it into a byte-level one with a relatively short additional training run.
Both come close to matching the models they were derived from, and Bwen 8B is our strongest byteified model yet—outperforming Bolmo 7B across our aggregate evaluation suite.
Working at this level can improve a model’s understanding of fine-grained text structure, from whitespace to different writing systems, without tying it to a fixed vocabulary.
why_it_matters_hint: Researchers can adapt existing models to read raw text more flexibly, without training from scratch.
